GitHub - Artemarius/cuda-zkp-ntt: GPU-accelerated Number-Theoretic Transform for ZK-Proof generation. Targets the NTT bottleneck (91% of Groth16 prover time) via two CUDA optimizations: async double-buffered pipeline eliminating CPU-GPU transfer overhead, and IADD3-path Montgomery multiplication reducing finite-field instruction latency. BLS12-381, Ampere sm_86, Nsight-profiled. · GitHub (https://github.com/Artemarius/cuda-zkp-ntt)

L224:   * v1.6.0: 3-field NTT — BLS12-381 (15.1 ms), Goldilocks (3.6 ms, 4.2x faster), BabyBear (2.4 ms, 6.2x faster) at n=2^22
L225:   * 15.5 ms at n=2^22 — 38% faster than v1.1.0 via radix-8 outer stages (Montgomery)
L226:   * Barrett + Montgomery dual arithmetic: Barrett NTT eliminates 12% Montgomery conversion overhead
L227:   * Batched NTT: process 8 independent NTTs in 3-4 kernel launches (vs 32 sequential); 1.52x throughput at 2^15
L228:   * 1.66x pipeline speedup at 2^18 via 3-stream async double-buffered NTT
L248: A 3-stream double-buffered NTT pipeline using CUDA streams, `cudaMemcpyAsync`, and `cudaStreamWaitEvent` for cross-stream dependencies. Dedicated streams for H2D transfers, NTT compute, and D2H transfers enable maximum overlap across the GPU's copy and compute engines.
L249: 
L250:     `H2D Stream:    |--H2D(0)--|--H2D(1)--|--H2D(2)--|--H2D(3)--|
L251:     Compute[0/1]:       |--NTT(0)--|--NTT(1)--|--NTT(2)--|--NTT(3)--|
L252:     D2H Stream:              |--D2H(0)--|--D2H(1)--|--D2H(2)--|--D2H(3)--|
L253:     `
L254: ### Direction B — Optimized Finite-Field Arithmetic
L255: 
L256: A from-scratch Montgomery multiplication kernel for the BLS12-381 scalar field (255-bit prime), targeting the `IADD3` instruction path. ZKProphet §IV-C shows that 70.8% of FF_mul instruction mix is `IMAD` (4-cycle issue latency) vs `IADD3` (2-cycle). Converting the critical path reduces stall cycles and increases integer pipeline utilization.
L257: 
L258: Key implementation choices:
L259:   * 8-limb 32-bit Montgomery representation for the 255-bit BLS12-381 scalar modulus
L260:   * Fused multiply-add using PTX `mad.lo.cc` / `mad.hi.cc` intrinsics
L261:   * Conditional reduction branchless via predicated instructions
L262:   * Roofline-validated against NVIDIA A-series integer throughput ceiling
L263: 
L264: * * *
L265: ## Performance Results
L266: 
L267: > Profiling conducted on NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (Ampere, 30 SMs, CUDA 12.8). Reference baseline: bellperson NTT (radix-256 Cooley-Tukey).
L268:

L271: --- | --- | --- | --- | ---

L273: v1.1 Montgomery (fused K=10 + coop outer)  | 1.21 ms  | 5.51 ms  | 25.1 ms  | 1.04x
L274: v1.2 Barrett (no Montgomery conversion)  | 1.27 ms  | 5.61 ms  | 24.9 ms  | 1.05x
L275: v1.3 4-Step (Bailey's algorithm)  | 1.66 ms  | 7.03 ms  | 29.5 ms  | 0.89x
L276: v1.4 Montgomery (branchless + radix-4)  | 0.952 ms  | 4.11 ms  | 17.1 ms  | 1.54x
L277: v1.4 Barrett (branchless + radix-4)  | 1.02 ms  | 4.39 ms  | 17.4 ms  | 1.51x
L278: v1.5 Montgomery (radix-8 outer)  | 1.75 ms  | 5.53 ms  | 15.5 ms  | 1.70x
L279: v1.5 Barrett (radix-4, unchanged)  | 1.93 ms  | 5.86 ms  | 17.5 ms  | 1.50x

L307: 
L308: On-the-Fly Twiddle Computation — Negative Result (v1.5.0):
L309: OTF twiddle computation (replacing 64 MB precomputed table with ~1 KB constant memory) was fully implemented (12 kernel variants, 16 tests) but is catastrophically slower for BLS12-381: 56.9 ms OTF vs 15.6 ms precomputed (+265%). Root cause: 256-bit binary exponentiation requires ~29 Montgomery muls per butterfly (~4480 MADs) vs 7 DRAM reads (224 bytes). Infrastructure retained for future multi-field work (Goldilocks/BabyBear where mul is 1-2 instructions). See 【105†analysis】.
L310: 4-Step NTT — Negative Result (v1.3.0):
L311: 
L312: The 4-step NTT (Bailey's algorithm) was fully implemented and tested (221 tests) but is slower than the cooperative approach at all sizes. At n=2^22: 29.5 ms (4-step) vs 24.9 ms (Barrett) = +18%. Root cause: 3 transpose passes add DRAM overhead; sub-NTTs of 2048 elements still have 1 cooperative outer stage hitting DRAM. See 【106†analysis】.
L313:

L315: Metric  | FF_mul (isolated)  | NTT Naive Butterfly  | NTT Fused (radix-256)
L316: --- | --- | --- | ---
L317: Bottleneck  | Memory (92% DRAM)  | Memory (79%)  | Compute (69%)
L318: Compute Throughput  | 64%  | 45%  | 69%
L319: ALU Pipe Utilization  | 44.5%  | 41.5%  | 67.3%
L320: Executed IPC  | 1.87  | 1.56  | 2.41
L321: Top Warp Stall  | Long Scoreboard (mem)  | LG Throttle (mem)  | Math Pipe Throttle

L323: The fused radix-256 kernel transforms the workload from memory-bound to compute-bound — data lives in shared memory across 8 butterfly stages, eliminating global memory round-trips and saturating the integer ALU pipe.
L324: 
L325: Direction B — SASS Instruction Reduction (cuobjdump, sm_86 Release):
L326: FF Operation  | Baseline SASS  | Branchless v2  | Reduction  | Technique
L327: --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L328: `ff_add`  | 127  | 55  | -57%  | PTX carry chain + LOP3 MUX, enables 128-bit vectorized loads
L329: `ff_sub`  | 94  | 55  | -41%  | `sub.cc` chain + `lop3.b32` replaces ISETP+SEL comparison
L330: `ff_mul`  | 571  | 527  | -8%  | Branchless conditional reduction (CIOS loop unchanged)
L331: `ff_sqr`  | 563  | 511  | -9%  | Same as ff_mul (sqr = mul(a, a))

L336: * * *
L337: ## v5.0.0 — GEMM-NTT (ConvKyber Approach)
L338: 
L339: ConvKyber-inspired approach: replace entire NTT butterfly stages with a dense 16x16 matrix multiply on Tensor Cores. The DFT-16 matrix Z[i][j] = omega_16^(i*j) encodes 4 butterfly stages into one GEMM.
L340: 
L341: Key difference from v4.0.0 element-wise TC: v4.0.0 replaced individual modular multiplies with WMMA (16 WMMAs per element, 50+ instructions vs 3-5 scalar). GEMM-NTT amortizes WMMA across 16 elements simultaneously — one GEMM replaces 32 butterfly operations.
L342: DFT-16 stage throughput (GEMM vs full scalar NTT):
L343: 
L344: Batch  | n=2^12  | n=2^14  | n=2^16  | n=2^18
L345: --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L346: B=8  | 0.05x  | 0.22x  | 0.19x  | 0.23x
L347: B=16  | 0.18x  | 0.31x  | 0.33x  | 0.33x
L348: B=64  | 0.42x  | 0.57x  | 0.51x  | 0.44x
L349: B=256  | 0.47x  | 0.75x  | 0.85x  | 0.63x
L350: 
L351: Ratio = GEMM DFT-16 stage time / full scalar NTT time. The DFT-16 stage handles 4 of log_n butterfly stages (22-33% of total work). Ratios < 1.0 mean the TC stage is faster than the corresponding fraction of scalar NTT.

L551: ## Context & Related Work
L552: 
L553: This project is directly motivated by three papers:
L554:   * ZKProphet (Verma et al., IEEE IISWC 2025) — systematic GPU performance characterization of ZKP proof generation, identifying NTT as the dominant bottleneck post-MSM optimization
L555:   * cuZK (Lu et al., TCHES 2023) — efficient GPU implementation of zkSNARK with novel parallel MSM via sparse matrix operations and async data transfer
L556:   * MoMA (Zhang & Franchetti, 【110†ACM CGO 2025†arxiv.org】) — Multi-word Modular Arithmetic code generation achieving 13× over ICICLE for 256-bit NTTs and near-ASIC performance on commodity GPUs via Barrett reduction and batched NTT processing
L557: The optimization targets (async NTT pipeline, IADD3-path FF_mul) are explicitly called out as open problems in ZKProphet §V-B. v1.2.0 adopts MoMA-inspired Barrett arithmetic and batched NTT processing. v1.3.0 implements the 4-step NTT (Bailey's algorithm) — a negative result that demonstrates transpose overhead exceeds outer-stage savings on consumer GPUs. v1.4.0 achieves a 32% speedup via branchless arithmetic and radix-4 outer stages, plus a CUDA Graph API.
L558: v1.5.0 pushes to 38% faster via radix-8 outer stages (Montgomery only; Barrett radix-8 disabled due to I-cache thrashing at 174 registers). v1.6.0 adds Goldilocks (Plonky2/3) and BabyBear (RISC Zero) NTT implementations, demonstrating that smaller fields achieve 4-6x speedup at proof-relevant sizes. v1.7.0 implements Plantard reduction — another negative result (+79% vs Montgomery for 256-bit fields).
L559: v2.0.0 adds all remaining Groth16 primitives (Fq/Fq2, G1/G2, MSM, polynomial ops) and an end-to-end toy prover. v2.1.0 delivers production MSM with signed-digit recoding, CUB radix sort, and parallel bucket reduction — 35.8x speedup at n=2^18. v2.2.0 adds Fibonacci circuits with sparse R1CS (COO format), Lagrange basis trusted setup via batch inversion, and a 2-stream batch pipeline — GPU wins 55-139x over CPU.
L560: v3.0.0 completes the full BLS12-381 pairing pipeline (Fq6/Fq12 tower, Miller loop, final exponentiation) and Groth16 verification via multi-Miller loop, enabling end-to-end setup-prove-verify. v4.0.0 systematically evaluates hardware acceleration paths: L2 cache residency for twiddle factors, read-only cache loads, software prefetch for MSM, INT8 Tensor Core NTT (negative: 2-12x slower for 31-bit field), multi-stream H2D overlap, and RT Core feasibility (all negative).
L561: v5.0.0 implements the ConvKyber GEMM-NTT approach — replacing 4 butterfly stages with a dense DFT-16 matrix multiply on Tensor Cores (unsigned char WMMA). The DFT-16 stage achieves 0.05-0.85x of full scalar NTT time, demonstrating that the GEMM approach is viable when amortized across 16 elements (unlike v4.0.0's element-wise approach). See 【101†NTT_OPTIMIZATION_ROADMAP.md】 for the full optimization roadmap.
